[h1]Fix Crash On Startup (v1.4.0.0)[/h1]

If the game crashes on startup, go to Steam > Library > Celeste > Right-click > Properties > Game Versions & Betas > Click "opengl" > Update, and restart the game.

Also, press "C" to close the title screen; that is not a copyright icon.

[h1] 8 Years Later and Reaching the Summit still makes me cry [/h1]

I played this game on my Nintendo Switch back in 2018. Bought it again when the physical run happened. Played through the Base Game, B and C Sides, and Completed the Farewell Chapter (Just, not on Steam at the time of writing).

[h3] This is a [i]Perfect[/i] Game [/h3]

A word I don't through around lightly, even with some of my absolute favorites.

The amount of a personal connection I had going through this game was something I had never experienced in video games. The emotional highs and lows and how it's integrated in gameplay; characters and their motivations; the level design. So many things about this game just work. Sure, it may be a more universal thing, but it [i]felt[/i] personal.

It's difficulty is incredibly balanced. Every single death, every mistake, always felt like it was my own. But as long as I preserved, to never let this mountain beat me, I knew I could do it. It's this ludo-narrative harmony that I find is so rare for me that only a small handful of games really accomplish.

Music so emotionally resonate I bought the soundtrack, something I [i]never[/i] do.

It's pixel art direction is spectacular. Enough information is conveyed and nothing feels overdesigned.

I'm so happy I can leave a proper review for a game that to this day is my favorite game of all time.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the platforming controls feel responsive and smooth, featuring mechanics like climbing and dashing.

citations.review_text: Absolutely killer game. Gameplay flows very smoothly and feels so satisfying.

Genuinely amazing gameplay, the satisfaction you get from this games movement mechanics are so special.  The game's story and pixel art are beautiful- you can tell there was real care put it into the character's animations as well. The music was perfect too and reaching the peak of Celeste couldn't have felt like more of an achievement; as it should. Great game, support it. BEWARE though, this game is seriously hard, do not go in looking for an easy time, but it is rewarding to see it through.

I actually hate platformers. I never feel like I'm in control of the character, either they feel too slidy, or too floaty, and it makes me frustrated. But this game makes me think I don't actually dislike the genre. You feel in control, always. Missed a platform? It's okay, cause you can just hold onto it and climb it. Too far? That's okay, cause you can just dash. It's actually not a hard game. The difficulty just comes from the level design rather than frustratingly precise jumps. And the design is good. Respawning immediately is awesome. Plays like a dream.

So, I actually wanted to get this game for personal reasons. I felt the story resonated with me a lot, so I got it. I was certain I was gonna die repeatedly and be unable to finish and end up growing frustrated with it, but that didn't happen. The game design made sure I had a fair experience throughout. Some secrets are really hard to find, but the main game is actually quite easy. But, back to the story. It's awesome. It's both deep and simple. A lot of people misinterpret it, I find, but I'm not gonna get into that. Either way, it's good.

The music is fantastic, and so is the graphic presentation. There's a lot of stuff to find. Overall it's just a great game. That should be known by now. And it's well-deserved, I'd say.
Fantastic art, a simple but meaningful story that backs a great feeling game. All the platforming feels like an extension of the last part you just learned and flows amazingly.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's movement mechanics as fluid, tight, and responsive, with precise platforming controls.

citations.review_text: Didn't turn me into a girl like it did for some other players but it is still an incredible game with an amazing stroy and top tier controls.

celeste sits at the peak of indie platforming and has set new standards for the benchmark of indie development

mechanically, this game feels so smooth. you can precisely predict where you will land way before you even press your input keys. that's an example of good core design.

each room feels challenging and rewarding to complete and as you progress further into celeste, the rooms can get extremely difficult. every chapter introduces new mechanics which tests your newfound abilities in passing different sections. it's the ultimate platforming experience.

you can have a 9/10 game, but a good sound design can push that game to a 10, even beyond that, which is exactly what the ost achieved. incredible heartfelt ost that was present in every aspect of the game and range of sound effects that tickle that section of your brain.

celeste is about climbing a mountain. a mountain deep inside all of us, that we need to overcome by loving ourselves, accepting yourself for who you are. i know the act of climbing celeste mountain will resonate with a lot of people out there.

it is mechanically challenging. there's no doubt about that. i hope you will enjoy this game as much as i did. i hope you can persevere and see what message this game tries to tell. i hope this game lingers in your mind for months and years to come. because it is beautiful.

this game was collecting dust in my library for too long, 1 because i kinda forgot and 2 i didn't know what to expect/hearing it was really hard had me hesitating to start this long journey. But thank god i did cause what followed was a masterpiece of a game and the most fulfilling experience i have had in a long time playing a game.

the goal is simple, climb the mountain but damn that task is hard, playing through celeste not only tests your mechanical skills in platforming but also mentally. Get ready to die thousands of times and sure it's frustrating at times but when you complete a level/world the amount of accomplishment was next level. the movement is fluid and fun, the music is peak and the story hits real hard brings a tear too my eye. 

I decided to 100% celeste and while it was one of the hardest things i've done in gaming, it really pushed me into doing what i thought was impossible, i am so glad i played this game and i recommend it to anyone that wants to play a game that tests their skills and limits in gaming, you'll be glad you did i promise. If you want to 100% aswell i wish you luck soldier, the secret achievements are a different beast but it is possible. You can do this.
I enjoyed celeste from every aspect, the music is good, the controls are great, the level Design is good but hard, great game.

I LOVE THIS GAME SO MUCH!!1 I recently 100%ed and it almost never felt like a chore, it was always just something to look forward to (except summit c side fuck that)
If you like platforming, you will ADORE this game. There's literally nothing to criticise about this game imo. The artstyle is so pretty to look at, the soundtrack is full of bangers and the storyline is inspiring and heartwarming. The gameplay is just perfect. Despite my horrible keybinds, movement feels so fluid and never unfair.
It is a difficult game, but I found the difficulty progression to be scaled well. However, even if you do struggle, there is an in-depth assist mode that you can tweak to your own preferences to still enjoy the game.
I've only just dipped my toes into the Strawberry Jam collab but there definitely seems to be a ton of modded maps to try after you beat the game as well :D
PLAY THIS GAME PLAY THIS GAME PLAY THIS GAME
Pretty much the only good platformer on the market imo, due to the non floaty, and tight movement.

As of writing, i just finished my 100% yesterday, and will be starting modded content tomorrow.

I already had a high opinion of celeste when i beat 7A 2 years ago, and knew id come back to it for the 100% eventually.

Seems like this past week or so was the prophesized time, as i started a new file a quickly beat the A-sides, before moving onto the B-sides, C-sides, and finally Farewell + Moon Berry.

Now? Celeste is my 4th favourite game of all time, with a solid argument for #3. Its the only other game that, imo, is a near perfect masterpiece nigh unparalleled. The movement is just *mwah*, absolutely flawless. The OST is gorgeous. The difficulty curve is a masterclass in of itself. And the story is beautiful.

Play Celeste. Even if you dont like platformers, just try it, worst case you dont like it and can refund it <2h.
I even have my mom playing Celeste, it's just that great. (they suck at it, but they are trying).
If you dont like Celeste? Well, im sorry for your loss, maybe watch a video on it or smth, cause the story and OST alone are worth a listen.

I love this game, i dont intend to stop playing it anytime soon, theres so much community created content, not to mention goldens if i ever decide to get those in future. The sheer brilliance and amount of stuff you get for however much Celeste costs is insane, even just including the base game, or hell even just the A-sides for those who dont like the challenge of the B and C-sides.

Play Celeste. Go on, do it. Stop looking at reviews. Go buy the game. Now!

Brilliant game that ties together responsive and rewarding gameplay, an amazing soundtrack, and a touching story. Would absolutely recommend; Easily one of the best indie games I've had the pleasure of playing.

citations.review_text:
[b]I will always recommend Celeste to anyone looking for a great platformer, even if you're new to the genre.[/b]

There are so many techniques (100+ or so that you can learn at your own pace) that the game turns into a fun, high octane puzzle with multiple solutions. Music is great and immersive right beside it's complex and dynamic characters and although I'm not personally a fan of the story, it's loved by many. 

With Celeste being my first platformer it took me 69 hours to 100%, but because of easy to download mods, goldening/deathless runs, speedrunning, and bingo just to name a few, I feel like I've barely scratched the surface at 255 hours.

Play Strawberry Jam. Get Olympus mod launcher and play Strawberry Jam. Also play the D-Sides. Trust me, they're good. It's why I have 500 hours in this game. Play Strawberry Jam. Also other stuff like Glyph. By the way, play Strawberry Jam.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as difficult and challenging, with later stages such as B-sides, C-sides, and chapter 9 testing player skill.

citations.review_text: It's rare for a game to nail both the story and gameplay to create something that's hard to put down, but Celeste is that game. The game is a bit difficult especially as you go to the newly added chapters or the secret sides, but I happily spent hours and hours to complete everything I could. Even without the story, I probably would have been hooked to play this game over and over. And talking about the story, I never had something that hit me as impactful as this game. Climbing a mountain is the objective of the main game, but it is a symbol of the obstacles you need to overcome along the way of feeling like your true self. Even the additional material of the game continues to go on from how even after feeling like yourself, there is still obstacles to maintain feeling mentally healthy or instances in which your mental health and your journey will be tested. I can honestly say, this game changed my views on my own life for the better and I will forever be grateful I was recommend this on a random workday.

I love this game dearly. First time I've been able to play a game so hard and not rage at all...well, at least up until Chapter 8 and the B-Sides.
The music and atmosphere is so beautiful and calming. The visuals are gorgeous, the gameplay feels better then anything I've ever played before, and the story is so real and inspiring and...I just love this game, man. Genuinely my favorite game ever.
The first time I played it, I got stuck on Chapter 9 and the C-Sides. But, after coming at it a second time, I finally overcame the struggle and 100%'ed the game...except for the goldens. I can't.
The only possible critique I could make is Chapter 1's music. It's lovely, like the rest of the soundtrack, but it can get irritating fast and the B-Side is worse. But I never muted it because it's still good.
Definitely a must try. 10/10

After 100% the game it left me shocked like Wow.. This game is insane. The soundtracks are insane. The story is sad yet fun to go through. All 175 Berries are phenomenal. All 35 chapters are phenomenal too. The gameplay is so fluid and fun that you don't realize that you are dying so many times.
The time needed to 100% this is crazy, you should expect around 250 to 300 hours of playtime if you are going for 100%. If you are just casually playing for berries and the main chapters expect 5 to 7 hours for main game and add 1 to 3 hours for all the berries on main game.
There is a ton of gameplay after the main game, you could go for true ending if you think your up to the challenge you can beat all B-sides or C-sides. there's also Pico 8 but it doesn't last long at all.
The Modding community is also insane for celeste if you are post-game fully consider strawberry jam for mods and more tech usage. If you don't want to do not want modded post game speed-running is always an option.
The graphics are also so so so good. I'm not a huge fan of pixel art but this game has outdone it at such a high level its insane to make me like it.

In conclusion if your planning to buy this game I think that's a great idea. It is not for an easy heart this game is difficult.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the learning curve is accessible to beginners, guiding players through the mechanics from the start.

citations.review_text:
[b]I will always recommend Celeste to anyone looking for a great platformer, even if you're new to the genre.[/b]

There are so many techniques (100+ or so that you can learn at your own pace) that the game turns into a fun, high octane puzzle with multiple solutions. Music is great and immersive right beside it's complex and dynamic characters and although I'm not personally a fan of the story, it's loved by many. 

With Celeste being my first platformer it took me 69 hours to 100%, but because of easy to download mods, goldening/deathless runs, speedrunning, and bingo just to name a few, I feel like I've barely scratched the surface at 255 hours.

Before playing Celeste, I haven't touched platformers and wouldn't have considered playing the genre at all. After playing Celelste, I would consider myself someone who is pretty competent at platfomers and I am interested in looking to other games like A Hat in TIme, Super Meat Boy, and Shovel Knight. The game is very accesible to people who haven't played a single platformer in their life, and will guide you through until you've mastered its mechanics. 10/10, worth the fulll price, and if you don't have the cash for that it goes on sale regularly.
Very linear and beginner-friendly learning curve
